To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) calibration is important for classifier combination, (2) calibration is more important for combination than for single model evaluation, (3) non-monotonicity is better than monotonicity for classifier combination, and (4) calibration before combination is better than after combination.

(a) the calibration of the individual models is important, but the calibration of the combined model is more important; (b) calibration before combination is better than calibration after combination; and (c) calibration before and after combination can improve performance.

i) calibration is a necessary step for the use of classifier combination in real-world applications, and ii) non-monotonicity is a better approach than monotonicity when calibrating the probabilities of the individual models to be combined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of calibration before and/or after combination and the choice of calibration method.
the use of calibration before and/or after combining classifiers, and the choice of the best evaluation measure to assess the performance of the resulting combination.
the following questions: (1) What is the effect of calibration before and/or after combination on the performance of classifier combination?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calibration before classifier combination is not recommended, but it can be beneficial after it.
the use of calibration is recommended for the combination of classifiers, but not before.
the use of calibration before classifier combination is recommended, while the use of calibration after combination is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calibration should be applied before combination if the aim of the combination is to improve probability estimation.
calibration should be done after combining classifiers, but before evaluating them.
, in general, it is better to calibrate the models individually before combination, and that the use of non-monotonic methods is recommended for the best performance of classifier combination.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to improve classifier combination, calibration methods should be used in the combination process, and not only in the evaluation of the results, and that the best calibration method is a new non-mononotonic method.
the use of calibration is a must for classifier combination and that calibration is more important than the choice of the combination method.
the use of calibrated probabilities is beneficial in classifier combination, and that the calibration of the probabilities should be done after combining the models.
